haiku-low.q1: Three consecutive breaching evaluations (5xx rate above 2% with at least 500 requests) while no unresolved incident exists for that service and rule.
haiku-low.q2: Each further breach is recorded as an incident_breach row on that incident. It pages nobody.
haiku-low.q3: Rate below 1% for 10 consecutive minutes resolves it. A later breach opens a new incident only after 3 fresh consecutive breaches.
haiku-low.q4: Primary is paged immediately, secondary 5 minutes later, then engineering manager 5 minutes after that, the last level. Any acknowledgement stops it.
haiku-low.q5: Push is tried first, then SMS for the same page. If both fail, it retries with backoff while unacknowledged; the escalation clock is unaffected.
haiku-low.q6: Everyone who was paged gets a resolved notice. Unsent pages are cancelled and escalation stops, even if nobody acknowledged.
haiku-low.q7: In the alert_state row (breach_streak, recovery_streak). A breach resets recovery_streak, a non-breach resets breach_streak, and a gap resets both.
haiku-low.q8: Each takes a SELECT FOR UPDATE lock on the alert_state row. If last_eval_minute is already at least t, the second rolls back. A unique partial index on incident backstops duplicate incidents.
haiku-low.q9: The dispatcher claims open incidents whose next_escalation_at is due and inserts a page for the next level. The unique (incident, level) constraint prevents a double page.
haiku-low.q10: The provider calls a signed webhook with the page id. The sender locks the incident, sets it acknowledged with next_escalation_at NULL, and cancels unsent pages.
haiku-low.q11: At send time, the on-call service is asked who holds that level's role right then. The result is stored as target on the page row.
haiku-low.q12: It reads the target stored on the page rows for the incident, and builds one resolved notice per distinct target.

sonnet.q1: 3 consecutive breaching evaluations (5xx rate over trailing 5 min above 2% with at least 500 requests in the window), and no unresolved incident already exists for that (service, rule).
sonnet.q2: Further breaches are recorded as incident_breach rows on the existing incident and page nobody (duplicate suppression); no new incident is opened.
sonnet.q3: It resolves automatically once the rate has stayed below 1% for 10 consecutive minutes (recovery_streak reaches 10). A later breach opens a new incident after 3 fresh consecutive breaching evaluations.
sonnet.q4: Primary at t0 (when the incident opens), secondary at t0+5 min, engineering manager at t0+10 min (the last level), unless acknowledged or resolved first.
sonnet.q5: Push fails or times out: SMS is sent for the same page (a duplicate is possible). If both fail, the page is retried with backoff while the incident is open and unacknowledged. A failed page never stops or delays the escalation clock.
sonnet.q6: Everyone who was paged (each distinct target on pages already attempted) gets a resolved notice (push, SMS fallback). Pending escalation stops: next_escalation_at is set to NULL and unsent pages are cancelled, even if nobody acknowledged.
sonnet.q7: In the alert_state table row for (service, rule): breach_streak, recovery_streak and last_eval_minute. Streaks reset on a non-qualifying evaluation (a breach resets recovery_streak; a rate below 1% resets breach_streak; 1% to 2% or too few requests resets both; zero-request windows leave recovery unchanged), and a gap (a minute neither evaluator evaluates) resets both.
sonnet.q8: Each evaluator opens a transaction and locks the alert_state row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; if last_eval_minute >= t the other already processed that minute, so it rolls back. A unique partial index on incident (one unresolved per service, rule) is the backstop that makes a second incident insert fail.
sonnet.q9: The stored deadline incident.next_escalation_at: dispatchers poll every few seconds for open incidents where it is <= now (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED). The step does not decide whether to send; it unconditionally inserts the page row for the next level (unique on incident and level), sets current_level and advances the deadline by 5 min, regardless of earlier push/SMS outcomes. Ack or resolution set the deadline NULL so nothing is due.
sonnet.q10: The responder taps Acknowledge in the provider's app; the provider calls our signed webhook with the page id; the page sender verifies the signature, locks the incident row, and if open and not yet acked sets status = acknowledged, acked_by, next_escalation_at = NULL and cancels unsent pages. Duplicates and acks on resolved incidents are no-ops. Racing with an escalation is resolved by the row lock: whichever commits first wins.
sonnet.q11: At send time, when the page sender processes the page: it asks the on-call service who holds the role for that level right now, not when the incident opened.
sonnet.q12: On resolve, the evaluator inserts a notice for each distinct target on pages already attempted; the target is stored on the page row (the record of who was paged), and the sender takes pending notices from the DB.
